note: Every line here is waiting on the author. The game shows the English string until the Hebrew is filled in.

strings.en: Walk the courts as the measurements describe them.
strings.why: One-line tagline on the front end. The author has his own phrasing for what the reconstruction claims; this is his sentence to write, not mine.
strings.suggestion: הלך בחצרות כפי שהמידות מתארות אותן.

strings.why: Numbered save slot label. Israeli usage is split between "משבצת" (literal) and "קובץ שמירה" (save file); this is the author's call and it appears on every slot card.
Button that writes to the first free slot. Wording depends on the choice made for save.slot.
Progress readout. "Stop" on a walking tour has several Hebrew renderings (תחנה / עמדה / נקודה) and the author has a preferred one.

strings.en: You have visited every stop on the tour.
strings.why: Completion message. Congratulatory register in Hebrew is a matter of taste and this is the last line of the whole tour.

Title of the reference panel. "Codex" has no settled Hebrew equivalent; candidates are לקסיקון, מאגר ידע, אנציקלופדיה, ילקוט. The author, who wrote the book this is built from, should name his own reference section.
Name of the colour-grade preset row. "Look" is a photographic term of art; Hebrew photographers say either "מראה" or keep the English "לוק".
Rule-of-thirds overlay toggle. Photographic Hebrew here is unsettled.
Scalability level 3. Unreal's own Hebrew wording for this tier is not established and "אפית" reads oddly as a quality level.
Scalability level 4. Same problem as Epic; also needs to sort sensibly above it in the dropdown.
Post-process quality group. "עיבוד תמונה" is used but overlaps with image processing generally; some Israeli titles keep "פוסט-פרוססינג".
Lumen GI quality group. The Hebrew rendering of the rendering term is not settled and this project leans heavily on Lumen.
TSR / TAAU selector. Israeli players generally say the English word; a Hebrew coinage here risks being unrecognisable.
Quality tier of the upscaler. Depends on the choice made for options.upscaling.
Screen percentage slider. "אחוז מסך" is a literal translation that does not convey what the slider does.
Whether crouch/sprint style actions are held or toggled. "מתג" reads as a hardware switch; the natural Hebrew here is a UI-convention question.
Comfort turning in fixed increments. Borrowed from VR vocabulary that has no settled Hebrew.
Colour-blindness compensation selector.
Medical term. Hebrew clinical usage is a transliteration (דויטרנופיה) but the accepted spelling varies; wrong spelling of a medical term in an accessibility menu is a bad look.
Medical term; same problem as deuteranopia.
Medical term; same problem as deuteranopia.

glossary.why: The English gloss for each class of korban is a matter of the author's own terminology and he has settled wording in his book. Left for him.
Deliberately left without an English gloss. "sacrifice" and "offering" carry different connotations and the choice belongs to the author.
The twice-daily offering. English gloss left to the author for the same reason as korban.
